absent: Numeric identifiers for console and remote processor device types and size and multiport feature bits.
Numeric operation codes for device ready and port ready and port open and port remove and bad identifier handling.
Ceiling value for maximum port count.
Complete field layouts for device and port and queue helper and console configuration records.
Internals of receive and transmit queue callbacks and control work processing and queue priming and control transmission and port lifecycle and size helpers and buffer management.
Transport queue discovery and reset and break and callback enable and disable semantics.
Numeric values for Ethernet sizing and alignment and polling weight and fragment limits.
Field layouts for transport statistics families and generic queue statistics.
Character device number allocation and debug directory contents beyond creation.
Remote processor specific transport differences beyond feature exclusion.

findings.text: A cross module helper removes one unused buffer from a generic queue handle by converting it to the ring specific form and dispatching through the backend operation table, returning the backend supplied cookie to the caller.
A header helper enumerates every queue belonging to a device by walking the device owned queue list, exposing each queue object in turn for teardown or inspection loops.

Device bringup is entered through a probe routine shared by the console driver and the remote processor serial driver, responsible for allocating the device record and linking it both ways with the transport device and registering the character device and validating port count and creating queues and marking readiness and announcing presence.

Device teardown is entered through a remove routine shared by both drivers, responsible for unlinking global state and draining deferred work and resetting the transport and unplugging ports and deleting queues and freeing the device record.

Queue and configuration events are entered through lightweight callbacks that only schedule deferred work, with control queue activity scheduling control handling and non multiport configuration changes scheduling size handling, while the size work handler resolves its device record from the work item and refreshes legacy size.

Power suspend and resume are entered through freeze and restore callbacks attached only to the console driver, with freeze quiescing transmit and disabling callbacks and discarding queue state, and restore rebuilding queues and rebinding ports and rearming receive paths and reannouncing open state.

Module lifetime is entered through an init routine that registers a port class and creates a debug directory and initializes global lists and registers both drivers with unwind on failure, plus an exit routine that reclaims DMA buffers and unregisters drivers and class and removes debug state.

Queue provisioning uses two queues for a single port device and twice the sum of port count plus one control pair for multiport, always placing port zero input and output first for older peer compatibility, then the control pair, then remaining ports in identifier order, with matching callback and name assignments.

Remote processor serial transport never consults size or multiport capability, while ordinary console transport consults size only for legacy single port operation and consults multiport to decide queue topology and deferred work selection.

Legacy resizing reads column and row values from device configuration and applies them solely to the port with identifier zero through lookup and size update and console resize steps, and does nothing when multiport or remote processor mode or missing size capability applies.

Port capacity defaults to one and stays single port unless a multiport capability read succeeds on non remote processor transport, in which case a zero value or a value above the implementation ceiling is rejected as invalid and otherwise multiport mode is enabled.
Probe requires configuration accessors to be present whenever size or multiport capability is offered, rejecting the device otherwise before any allocation.

Control transmit completions carry a pointer to a device owned control packet rather than heap port buffers, so teardown drains them without invoking the generic buffer free path, while all other queues flush active buffers and detach plus free every unused entry.

Successful bringup always marks the transport ready before populating receive state, creates port zero directly for single port peers but prepopulates the control receive queue for multiport peers, publishes the device on the global list under protection, and finally announces device readiness with success indication plus a legacy size refresh.

Resume reuses the stored port list, rebinds each port to the freshly allocated input and output queues by identifier, refills each input path, queries host open state, and repeats guest open indication only for ports that were open at suspend, while the control receive queue is refilled only after the port loop completes and transmit gating is lifted last.

Offload bit translation treats only a small closed interval as mapped and leaves all other bits unchanged, adding a fixed delta derived from the feature base minus the offload base to mapped values to obtain the corresponding feature bit.
Transmit and receive tuning defaults enable checksum handling and segmentation offload and transmit polling, while the polling weight starts from the generic poll constant.

Queue statistics are described by paired descriptor tables that separate plain counters from queue API mapped counters, with send side plain entries covering datapath acceleration and kick and timeout events and receive side plain entries covering drops and acceleration and kicks, while mapped entries expose packet and byte totals plus stop and wake and hardware drop and checksum and segmentation and rate limit groups.

Console operation advertises size and multiport capabilities and matches the console device identifier with any sub identifier, while remote processor operation advertises no capabilities and matches the remote processor serial identifier only when remote processor support is compiled in, with both identifier tables terminated by an empty entry.

The global device list is mutated only while holding the global ancillary lock with interrupts disabled, covering both insertion at the end of successful probe and removal at the start of device teardown.

The per device port list has a dedicated lock that also coordinates suspend, where freeze holds it with interrupts saved while briefly acquiring and releasing each port transmit lock in turn to wait for in flight transmit paths before resetting the transport.

Multiport control paths have separate receive and transmit locks initialized only in multiport mode, with the transmit lock held while draining completed and unused control transmit entries during queue removal, and the receive lock supplied whenever the control receive queue is populated.

Each port carries independent input buffer and output queue locks passed to queue fill and transmit helpers, so input refills and output submission on different ports can proceed without sharing the device wide port list lock beyond list traversal.

A statistic descriptor holds a fixed length human readable name sized for generic string handling plus a byte offset into the local statistic storage and a second offset for queue API mapping where negative one means no mapping.

Send statistics combine a synchronization primitive with packet and byte totals and acceleration transmit and drop counts and kick and timeout and stop and wake counters, while receive statistics combine the same synchronization style with packet and byte totals and drop and acceleration packet and transmit and redirect and drop and kick counters, and a separate free path aggregate tracks packets and bytes split by polling context plus a dedicated acceleration pool counter.
Interrupt coalescing preferences are stored as a pair of thirty two bit limits for maximum packets and maximum microseconds.

A send queue record aggregates its transport queue pointer and a scatter list sized for maximum fragments plus linear and header entries and a sixteen character name and embedded send statistics and coalescing preferences and a polling context and a reset flag and an acceleration pool pointer plus a DMA address for its header area.

Driver descriptors bind feature tables with explicit sizes and human readable names and identifier tables to shared probe and remove routines, with the console descriptor additionally binding configuration change and suspend resume handlers while the remote processor descriptor omits them, and the character device operations table carries only module ownership.

Bringup progresses from configuration access validation through device record allocation and character device registration and capacity validation and lock and work initialization and queue creation to transport readiness, then diverges to control queue priming or direct port zero creation, and only after global publication announces readiness and refreshes size.

Removal progresses from global unlink under protection through transport break and deferred work flush and transport reset and synchronous work cancellation to per port unplug and character device unregistration and queue deletion with per queue yielding and finally device record release.

Suspend moves from transmit gating with release ordering through transmit drain and transport reset to callback disabling and work cancellation with a repeated control disable to cover handler rearming, then per port callback disabling and host state clearing and data removal and queue deletion, while resume reverses with queue rebuild and readiness and per port rebind and refill and host query before control priming and transmit ungating.

Interrupt context never performs slow work directly but only requests deferred handling, with control interrupts always deferring and configuration interrupts deferring solely for single port devices, and deferred handlers performing size refresh or control processing outside atomic context.

Bringup must handle missing queue memory and missing configuration access and out of range port capacity as terminal errors that unwind already acquired character device and memory state without publishing the device.

Failure to prime the multiport control receive queue after transport readiness is treated as a functional device failure that first notifies the peer with an unsuccessful readiness indication and then performs full removal before returning the error.

Priming the control receive queue before finishing the unprotected port rebind loop would let the peer deliver a removal message that mutates the same port list concurrently, risking use after free and list corruption, so the implementation defers control priming until after the loop.

Console writes can remain active across suspend, so freeze gates transmit paths with a release ordered flag and then drains each port transmit lock under the port list lock before resetting, and restore only clears the gate after all output queue pointers have been reassigned.

Treating control transmit cookies as heap port buffers would corrupt memory because they point to an embedded device packet, so removal uses a dedicated drain that detaches without freeing, unlike other queues that free every detached buffer.

Control handling can reenable its completion callback as its final step while racing with suspend, so freeze disables the callback both before and after synchronous work cancellation to ensure it stays disabled.
Mapped offload interval starts at 46 and ends at 47 inclusive, while mapped feature interval starts at 65, giving a translation delta of 19 added to mapped offload bits.

Favorable packet length is the sum of header plus virtual LAN header plus data payload constants, favorable copy length is 128, and receive padding is the sum of address alignment plus socket buffer padding constants.
Datapath acceleration transmit uses bit zero and redirect uses bit one, queue role identifiers are zero for receive and one for transmit and two for control, and the driver version string is 1.0.0.

Guest receive offload mask aggregates eight capabilities covering segmented TCP for version four and version six plus explicit congestion notification plus datagram fragmentation plus segmented UDP for version four and version six plus two mapped tunnel segmentation forms.

Statistic descriptors use negative one in the queue mapping offset to indicate no queue API mapping, with unmapped tables always using that sentinel and mapped tables supplying a real queue structure offset.
